column1: # Rule-by-rule correspondence between the published paper and this
# Why this file exists.  Four of this development's rules differ from the
# rules printed in the paper, and three of those differences went unnoticed
# until long after publication -- including one on which the paper's
# Theorem 1 fails as printed.  Nobody had ever computed the diff, because
# nothing required it.  This table does: tools/check-correspondence.sh
# fails the build if a rule of the mechanized semantics has no row here,
# so a rule cannot be added, weakened or strengthened without someone
# writing down what it does to the correspondence.
# Paper: Toya Makino and Tetsuo Yokoyama, "Small-Step Semantics with
# Meta-Level Reversibility for a Reversible Core Language", Reversible
# doi:10.1007/978-3-032-30839-9_12.  Figure and equation numbers below are
#   identical      same premises and conclusion, up to notation
#   extended       ours fires strictly more often than the printed rule
#   repaired       the printed rule is defective; ours differs deliberately
# Columns: paper_rule <TAB> paper_where <TAB> artifact <TAB> relation <TAB> note
